newsitem.title: UK: LME ALUMINIUM LEVITATING NEAR HIGHS, ZINC FIRM.
newsitem.headline: LME ALUMINIUM LEVITATING NEAR HIGHS, ZINC FIRM.

text.p: Aluminium hovered near fresh 22-month highs in Thursday morning LME ring trading as spreads flared and more speculative money poured in, but turnover was modest, traders said.
Zinc was also boosted by hot money, but forward selling tipped prices from their highs.
In aluminium, covering by players short of options, investment house buying and fund activity are mainly behind the recent jump in prices to fresh 22-month highs, traders said.

Three months aluminium hit a peak of $1,762 per tonne in pre-market trading, a $200 or 13 percent rise over the past three weeks. It ended the morning kerb at $1,758, a $16.50 gain from Wednesday's close.

The cash/threes spread widened as borrowers bid it up in the first ring. It traded at a $15 backwardation compared to $5/$10 indicated at Wednesday's close. October/threes came out $2 to a $5/$6 back.
"It's gone beyond the fundamentals, everyone's a bit wary at these heights," one floor trader said.
Another added: "People are concerned the market is overbought and have tight stops, but when more buying came in this morning, they had to join in."
The 14-day relative strength index was at 76 on Thursday morning, above the 70 level regarded as overbought.
Zinc climbed to a high of $1,557 on bank buying, the strongest since prices plummeted $300 last week from a seven-year high of $1,675.
With the backwardation holding up and prices at more reasonable levels, speculative money feels comfortable entering the market in the run-up to a squeeze in September, traders said.
But forward trade selling knocked prices back, ending the kerb at $1,539, a gain of $11.
Copper joined the party, gaining $16 to $2,314, breaking through resistance at $2,310.
The 10-day and 30-day moving averages at $2,320 and $2,328 respectively, however, may inhibit further rises, chartists noted.
The cash/threes backwardation, which came in on Wednesday to the narrowest since last October, widened about $7 to $27/$33.
Lead, which sunk to 22-month lows of $603 on Tuesday, recovered to $618, a gain of $12 from Wednesday.
Nickel consolidated at lower levels after Monday's losses, finishing the kerb $50 firmer at $7,210.
Tin added $10 to $5,600 while alloy shadowed the primary market and moved up to $1,540/48 from $1,530.
